newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open mostly unchanged Monday, dealers said.
Sugar losses from Cyclone Justin in Queensland, Australia, could exceed A$50 million, Ian Ballantyne, general manager of CANEGROWERS said in a statement today.
Annual production in North Queensland is A$500 million to A$600 million a year.
Turkey raised customs tax on sugar imports to 135 percent from 100 percent in an effort to curb imports. The increase is expected to begin immediately.
Friday, benchmark CSCE May closed down 0.07 cent at 10.83 cents per lb, having ranged from 10.92 to 10.81 cents. Volume was estimated at a light 7,478 lots.
Support remained at 10.68 cents in May and resistance at 11.05 cents.
LIFFE white sugar futures were slightly lower in thin trade as dealers awaited the open in New York. Benchmark May was trading $0.40 lower at $305.80, at 0900 EST/1400 GMT.
